items.title: Dick Spottswood interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 13, 2023
items.q: The interviewee mentions Johnny Hodges in the context of music history and royalty disputes involving Duke Ellington, but does not describe a personal interaction or direct professional relationship with Hodges himself.

ctx.x: But the 1-4-5, I’m sometimes surprised, if you look up blues on Wikipedia or in dictionaries, encyclopedias, to me the twelve-bar blues is the most elegant music form that I know of. And sometimes it gets short-shriffed in the definition of blues.

Uh yeah? I think blues also is more than that. I mean the twelve-bar blues, the call, the response and the — it’s like what’s his name, the thesis, the antithesis and the synthesis — who was the philosopher? Hegel. That’s nice as far as it goes but there’s music that’s branching out of that all over the place that’s just as traditional. I’ve discovered, here comes another plug for the Ma Rainey record. One of my little discoveries was the tune that Ma sings with the “Titanic Man Blues” and it goes [hums] and so…
That’s a useful phrase in research, “You’ve got me.”
